scope: Every selected current texture set, its declared component files and required views/states. Current failed horn v5 draft reviewed separately; no production model exists for it. Historical superseded attempts are indexed, not re-approved.

findings.observation: The assembled profile shows two offset dark circular contours around the visible hand, producing an extra crescent on its forward edge. This is visible in neutral and palette assemblies and in the overlay comparison.
findings.correction_principle: Reconcile hand compositing and contour ownership so the intended hand retains one clean outer boundary while preserving the cuff opening.

decision.reason: I inspected the assembled profile, original bare Irudad body and full item/overlay evidence. An additional hand crescent is visible in the robe assembly while the bare hand has one outline. It repeats the prohibited body/clothing ownership artifact and should be corrected before reusing this fit. Exact component-level cause remains to be traced during that correction.
decision.verification: Corrected single-item east/west assembly has one original hand contour, intact cuff and unchanged body/frame; fresh independent structural review after the correction.

findings.observation: The supplied PNG is the human-female comparison, with no Nima-specific assembled body visible. Its shared fitting screens clear on that mannequin, but these pixels cannot establish fit against the unfinished Nima mutation assembly.
findings.correction_principle: Provide an actual Nima assembled turnaround with the selected fitting before clearing the Nima-specific integration.

decision.reason: The shared bare-base fitting is intentional and does not establish that the named assembly is missing. I inspected the existing Nima all-view assembly and verified that it references this exact current fitted model. Hat/sole/ankle placement is present on Nima; no conflicting local attachment is established. The named assembly also receives its own independent review in this sweep.
decision.verification: Exact current model bindings checked; static assembled placement inspected. No native acceptance inferred.

findings.observation: The mattress is presented as a broad, almost plan-view rectangle in every direction, while its supporting frame collapses to perimeter lines and tiny end stubs. The side view does not expose a readable mattress side thickness or under-bed support volume. Compared with the requested shallow-top map camera, this reads as a flat overhead bed diagram rather than a raised bed on wooden slats.
findings.correction_principle: Retain the source fabric and head/foot arrangement, but reconcile the horizontal mattress plane with one shallow cardinal camera and show a continuous supporting rail/slat volume and readable clearance or feet where visible.

decision.reason: I inspected the converted all-view bed, its source description/camera contract and the actual installed VTE Bed_south reference. The donor itself uses a cardinal overhead sleeping plane, and the current packet explicitly records that camera and one continuous fabric pad on low slats. The white sleeping plane and thin low frame therefore do not establish an erroneous camera or missing support. Exposing an under-bed volume by changing the angle would contradict this selected reference. Rail readability could be cosmetic polish, but is not a structural correction to make now.
decision.verification: Source-supported low construction and actual directional donor camera inspected; no native test inferred.

findings.view: Fixed cardinal face, all three phases, neutral and source palette
findings.region: Right inset oval and light rectangular segments
findings.observation: The inset oval/segment assembly reads as a separate floating loop inside the outer wooden rim: no visible spoke or bridge joins it to the central spine or outer rim. The model explicitly calls this a source inset segment plane, so this is a readability/attachment uncertainty rather than proof that a hidden axle is absent or that the source silhouette must change.
findings.correction_principle: Check intended source role before changing geometry; if it is meant to be physically attached, make the existing attachment legible without inventing a new mechanism or erasing source openings.

decision.reason: I inspected all three neutral/native phases and the actual source packet. The right segmented oval visibly floats inside the larger wheel; source glyph occupancy supports its shape but does not establish how it attaches mechanically. I cannot substantiate a missing hidden axle, and will not invent a bridge from that assumption. This ambiguity affects the physical construction and should be resolved in Stage3 before treating the conversion as generation-ready.
decision.verification: Establish the inset component role and shared support/clearance geometry from source/reference; make the attachment legible or document evidenced occlusion, then inspect all three phases with the independent fast review.

findings.observation: A short rectangular raised plateau interrupts the otherwise long straight back contour in both profiles. The squared rise and drop read as a cropped/joined contour rather than continuous fur/anatomy; it remains visible in the composited native close-up.
findings.correction_principle: Reconcile the visible dorsal join into one deliberate continuous back contour, preserving the current body registration and pixel scale.

decision.reason: I inspected the neutral assembly and confirmed the small squared profile-back step. It is a connected contour bump, without detached anatomy, a pivot shift or an equipment intersection. Optional silhouette polish does not justify reopening the accepted Ray Cat shape ahead of structural fixes.
decision.owner_stage: Optional art polish outside required correction scope
decision.verification: Any later silhouette edit preserves the shared frame and receives independent structural review.

findings.observation: The lower apron changes abruptly from brown to yellow along a perfectly horizontal line, with no garment seam or border. Neutral shading is continuous across that line, so the native palette split reads as a rectangular detail-mask boundary rather than garment construction.
findings.correction_principle: Make the detail palette boundary follow a deliberate sewn panel/edge or integrate its transition into the apron material; retain independent equipment color ownership.

decision.reason: I inspected the native assembly, original apron glyph on the source comparison and source packet. The original has a distinct lower detail-color field; source rows17..21 deliberately map to that lower region. Native W is gold. The horizontal hue change preserves Qud identity; it is not unrelated body color leaking into clothing. Do not invent a seam or erase the source region.
decision.verification: Actual source lower color field and current native role mapping inspected.

findings.region: open / neutral and open / native y: left side of aperture
findings.observation: The narrow open leaf reads as a detached upright slab: a continuous visible ground gap separates its full height from the left jamb, and neither hinge nor attachment bridges that gap. At enlarged scale this weakens the mechanical reading of an attached open door; the small source mask establishes a narrow open leaf but does not establish this added arch-to-leaf relationship.
findings.correction_principle: Keep the fixed frame and state anchor, but make the open leaf visibly pivot from the hinge-side jamb through coherent hinge/edge geometry rather than floating inside the opening.

decision.reason: I inspected open/closed neutral/native states and source description. The open slab has a full-height gap to its jamb with no visible pivot connection. Closed hinge pieces also fail to explain attachment across that gap. Source text explicitly describes hinges. Preserve the common frame/state anchor and construct coherent hinge-side attachment.
decision.verification: Open/closed geometry shows a coherent fixed hinge attachment, unchanged frame/anchor and material roles; fresh independent all-state review.

findings.region: Uppermost canopy tuft, above and left of upper-right crown
findings.observation: The highest foliage cluster is surrounded by visible background and does not meet the neighboring foliage or a visible branch. It reads as a floating canopy island. The isolated wood plate supplies no visible connecting limb in this gap.
findings.correction_principle: Resolve the visible crown connection using source-appropriate branch or foliage continuity; do not rely on an imagined hidden support across exposed background.

decision.reason: I inspected neutral/native variant2 and the source description. The highest foliage tuft is separated by exposed background from its neighboring crown and visible branch system. It has no visible owning support; this is a source-appropriate crown/branch continuity defect to fix before further reuse. Preserve the two native crown variants and palette roles.
decision.verification: Variant2 upper crown has legible foliage/branch continuity without a floating island; variants, roots, frame and independent G/w tint remain intact; fresh structural review.

findings.view: Variants 1-3, neutral, ripe and unripe; clearest in Variant 3
findings.region: Basal stem and low curved strokes
findings.observation: Several low curved vine strokes do not visibly join their nearby upright stems. Most clearly, Variant 3 has a separate arc below the right stem with background between them; Variant 1 also leaves the long central upright above the low left curve. These curves read as detached plant fragments rather than continuous basal growth. Model/source describe living crooked vine layouts, not debris.
findings.correction_principle: Make intended basal growth visibly continuous with its owning vine, or establish its source-supported independent role; preserve the same corrected geometry in both harvest tints.

decision.reason: I inspected the neutral/ripe layouts and source description. Variant3 right stem visibly stops above its basal curve; other low strokes similarly fail to explain continuous growth. No source-supported debris or separate ground-object role is established. Resolve these basal contacts consistently in all three layouts and both harvest tints.
decision.verification: All intended basal contacts are continuous, or have an evidenced independent role; identical geometry/frame in ripe/unripe states and independent w/g/K roles; fresh all-layout review.

findings.observation: The visible horns form closed ram-like curls with tips descending beside the head. The supplied source description specifies grooved bone extrusions racing to a symmetrical point above the head; that pointed upward silhouette is not demonstrated by this plate.
findings.correction_principle: Reconcile the horn geometry with the authoritative source silhouette; preserve separate flesh ears and continuous crown attachment.

decision.reason: The user selected sheep/ram-like horns and has been reviewing that curl design. A generic natural Horns description does not override this explicit authored choice or require replacing it with straight spikes. The reviewer correctly asks for source reconciliation, but that does not add a new silhouette redesign. Existing independently confirmed crown-root, return-tip and skull-clearance defects remain open and keep horns unready.
decision.verification: Authored ram-like interpretation reconciled with user direction; separate structural horn correction still required.

findings.view: SOUTH, especially human-male and Irudad rows
findings.observation: Gray secondary sole-like arcs protrude beyond the dark front foot/sole contours, most conspicuously to the right of the male left-screen foot. They read as offset duplicate rim fragments rather than a single continuous sole; female/Nima rows show less of this.
findings.correction_principle: Inspect the visible sole/body ownership at these edges and retain one deliberate continuous sole silhouette, removing any duplicate source edge fragments.

decision.reason: I inspected the aggregate, male fit and intact-source plate. The gray arcs belong to the continuous whole outsole outside the original foot; the dark inner boundary belongs to the original toes/foot. No detached duplicate sole piece is established. The protruding rim could be made less conspicuous as optional polish, but should not be removed merely because the sole is wider than the bare foot.
decision.owner_stage: Optional art polish outside required correction scope
decision.verification: Continuous intact sole and foot/sole ownership inspected; no current structural blocker established.

limitations: Static generation-time screening, not native/game validation or a guarantee.
Component files were inventoried and checked for exact hashes; visual review is at rendered-set and targeted-component level, not a claim that all3253 component PNGs were individually inspected.
Superseded/rejected provenance is separately indexed rather than silently approved.

existing_critical_issues.reason: Fresh independent horn critique confirms flat-ended emergence, visually fragmented rear return and unresolved non-root skull clearance. User explicitly rejected rear curl and terminal cutoff. Broad retrospective screening does not override this closer evidence.
existing_critical_issues.verification: Continuous embedded crown roots, complete tip path and non-root skull clearance explained in every view; fresh review after next refinement before any extraction.
